newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGB futures end firmer, cash JGBs sold.
newsitem.headline: Key JGB futures end firmer, cash JGBs sold.

text.p: Key December Japanese government bond futures closed slightly higher on Friday after investors sold cash JGBs and bought futures, traders said.
"Investors are selling cash JGBs and buying futures," said a brokerage trader.
Sales of cash JGBs from investors capped the upperside, said a trader at a city bank's securities affiliate.
"Dealers saw that investors were selling 10-year cash JGBs, and dealers followed with sales of the benchmark cash JGB," the trader said.
The December closed at 123.33, up slightly from Wednesday's 123.27, and moved within a range of 123.15 to 123.44. Thursday was a national holiday and markets were closed.
Talk that an agricultural financial institution was selling 10-year cash JGBs pulled down the benchmark 182nd cash JGB, a trust bank trader said.
"There is talk that an agricultural financial institution has sold 10-year JGB brands in the 170th to the 179th zone, and this is weighing down the benchmark 182nd JGB," the trader said.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd cash JGB stood at 2.760 percent as of 0655 GMT, up from Wednesday's 2.740 percent.
A speech by Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita in the afternoon had little effect on the market because what he said was in line with his previous comments, traders said.
"The BOJ's monetary policy will continue to be geared to making a firmer basis for economic recovery," Matsushita said.
In the morning, the December rose slightly, amid expectations that investors would have to buy JGBs.
But hardly any such buying was seen in the market, partly because of the irregular schedule this week, with Thursday a national holiday.
The December fell in the early afternoon, due to sales of cash JGBs, traders said.
The key futures contract picked up toward the close, however, on short-covering by dealers, said a trader for a trust bank's securities affiliate.
